Reddit announced two upcoming changes that are likely to be quite unpopular with some of its more seasoned users.

The company has already imposed a restriction on old Reddit, and has now announced a second one. In addition, RSS support will also be discontinued…

Old Reddit

Reddit underwent a major interface overhaul in 2018, which provoked strong opposition from users who preferred the original version. In response to these voices, the platform committed at the time to continue offering what later became known as "old Reddit" for as long as people kept using it.

In August this year, the company required old Reddit users to log in first — that was the first policy change. Now they have announced that the original UI will be restricted to users who have used it within the past six months, and new users will no longer be able to access it.

Reddit says both measures are aimed at reducing AI scraping of the platform's content (although, if you're willing to pay, the problem apparently disappears).

RSS Feeds To Be Discontinued

The reason given for discontinuing RSS feeds is exactly the same.

For subreddits that rely on RSS for moderation work, this change could have a particularly large impact. Reddit says it is aware of the situation and suggests moderators switch to Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay.

Users Are Not Happy

A look at the comment section makes it clear that many long-time users are extremely unhappy with these latest developments.

What do you make of these latest changes? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
